title: Tightly-Coupled Message Protocols (Multitudinous Handler Explosion)
pattern: Defining distinct, fine-grained network message schemas and corresponding handler methods for every individual data attribute modification across separate application tiers.
why_bad: Adding a single field to the model requires updating all message schemas, modifying multiple serialization formats, and rewriting dozens of protocol handlers across three tiers, creating massive development friction and stopping refactoring [386].
detection: A high ratio of separate network message types to domain entities, combined with handlers that map directly to single attribute mutations.
counterexample: Valid for performance-critical systems where network bandwidth is extremely constrained and updates must be minimal. Mark as `Context-dependent`.
fix: Expose coarse-grained, document-based message protocols or use unified patch-delta payloads to allow cohesive data structures to flow seamlessly [386, 626].
source: Clean Architecture, Chapter 17, "boundaries: drawing lines" [386]; Designing Data-Intensive Applications, Chapter 4 [626]
